milestone_brief:
textbook-ingest-m11 (e5 part 2 of 2 — CLOSES e5 and the textbook-ingest epic) — Enforce the non-OA license-truncation policy: surface at most 300 chars of a non-open-access chunk's body via get_chunk, with a truncated_for_license:true flag; full text for open-access chunks.

CONTEXT: e5 part 1 (m10) finalized the PDF-hardening doc. This part adds the license-compliance truncation. The truncated_for_license flag is documented as a FUTURE flag (ingest/schema.py:165, ingest/chunker_types.py:129 say 'lands with e5') — it is NOT a schema column and NOT enforced yet. The license column (default 'arxiv-license') already round-trips per-chunk (m2): tiers seen are 'arxiv-license' (arXiv), 'GFDL' (Stacks Project), 'CC-BY'/'CC-BY-SA', 'author-distributed' (lecture notes), and 'no explicit license'. There is NO is_open_access helper or license allowlist yet — m11 must define one.

WHERE truncation applies: get_chunk (server/handlers/chunk.py) returns the full sanitized body_text with an EXISTING byte-cap body_truncated flag + resource_link path (E13_S04). m11 adds a DISTINCT, license-based 300-char truncation: for a non-OA chunk, slice body_text to <=300 chars and set truncated_for_license=true. CRITICAL ORDERING: the handler sanitizes body_text and wraps it in <retrieved_chunk> indirect-prompt-injection delimiters (E13_S02 Threat 2) BEFORE the byte-cap truncation — m11 must truncate the INNER body, NOT slice off the delimiter tags (mirror the existing sanitize-before-truncate ordering at chunk.py:69-74). The 150-char search_papers snippet (SNIPPET_MAX_CHARS=150) is already under 300, so search snippets need no length change — research should decide whether non-OA search rows should ALSO carry the truncated_for_license flag for transparency.

POLICY (the central decision — research to confirm, flag for operator if genuinely contested): define an OPEN-ACCESS ALLOWLIST of license tokens that get FULL text — recommend {arxiv-license, CC-BY, CC-BY-SA, CC0, public-domain, GFDL} (GFDL/CC-BY-SA are copyleft-open per the roadmap's Stacks Project tier) — and truncate everything else (author-distributed, copyrighted, unknown/empty) to 300 chars. FAIL CLOSED: an unknown/missing/empty license -> treat as non-OA (truncate). This is the safe default for copyright compliance. The roadmap [SHOULD] assumption (plans/textbook-ingest-roadmap.md line ~43) frames this as 'acceptable to operator'.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- get_chunk on an open-access chunk (e.g. license='arxiv-license') returns full body_text, truncated_for_license=false (or absent per the established absent-not-null pattern).
- get_chunk on a non-OA chunk (e.g. license='author-distributed') returns body_text sliced to <=300 chars + truncated_for_license=true.
- Unknown/empty license -> treated as non-OA (fail closed -> truncated).
- The 300-char license truncation composes correctly with the existing E13_S04 byte-cap body_truncated path (the two flags are independent; document precedence — license truncation should apply first/innermost so a non-OA chunk never leaks >300 chars even via the byte-cap/resource_link path).
- <retrieved_chunk> delimiter wrapping (E13_S02) preserved — truncate the inner body, not the tags.
- get_chunk result schema (server/schemas/get_chunk_result.json or equivalent) gains the truncated_for_license field; version bump in lockstep with TOOL_SCHEMA_VERSION; re-pin EXPECTED_TOOL_SCHEMA_SHA256 / EXPECTED_BP1_SHA256 ONLY if a tool DESCRIPTION/inputSchema actually changes (adding a result-envelope field alone does NOT change BP1 — recall the m9 lesson that BP1 hashes only {name, description} per tool; flag the precise re-pin scope).
- .claude/docs/snippet-contract.md updated to document the license-truncation policy + the OA allowlist + the flag + the precedence vs the byte-cap.
- Tests: OA chunk full text; non-OA chunk truncated to 300 + flag; unknown/empty license fail-closed; delimiter-preservation under truncation; composition with the byte-cap truncation; the is_open_access/allowlist helper unit tests.

CONSTRAINTS: assert banned for invariants (use if...raise); pure-ASGI; local-first; no anthropic SDK; doc placement under .claude/. This milestone CLOSES e5 and is the LAST textbook-ingest milestone.
